review_output: {"summary":"The repair fixes the prior MAJOR. In POST, the same-origin check and a 1,200/min per-source gate now run before parsing. Only requests that strictly parse as `action === \"open\"` use the separate 1,200/min open bucket. Malformed requests and all other mutations still use both the 1,200/min gate and the original 60/min `live-interactions` bucket. GET has its own 1,200/min bucket, and its limit check runs before the request is processed. The order of auth, admission (`admittedViewer` before any action), body bounds (`readJsonBody` after the source gate) and transactions is unchanged in the excerpts. The 32-viewer route test runs the real trusted resolver and memory limiter. It sends 960 opens and 960 GETs, then 60 writes that return 201 and a 61st that returns 429. The headroom is plausible for the stated 2-second polling. The nonpayment threshold matrix still holds for POST at 60, because the `{}` body fails to parse and goes to the 60/min bucket. On the client, the scripted POST now backs off on 429/503 while GET keeps polling, a GET 429/503 backs off everything, the Retry-After delay is limited to 2–60 seconds with a 30-second fallback, and the unmount cleanup is tested. I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR. There is one MINOR client regression: the last scripted run is now kept after failures other than 429/503. This review doesn't certify the full work package, deployment, commercial rate-limit providers, the business database, or the 8 action/helper files outside this scope.","findings":[{"severity":"MINOR","file":"src/components/live-advanced-interactions.tsx","area":"refresh(): lastScriptedRun / catch branch of the scripted open request","issue":"`lastScriptedRun` is meant to keep the last run visible only while the scripted POST is backing off. It is also kept when the open request fails for other reasons (409 ended/already joined, 5xx, network error). Then `setRun(scriptedRun ?? payload.runs?.[0] ?? null)` keeps showing the stale scripted run and hides manual runs from GET.","evidence":"Before this change, `scriptedRun` was reset to null on every tick, so any open failure fell back to `payload.runs?.[0]`, as the comment '排定事件已結束或暫時失敗，仍讀取手動互動與精選問題' says. Now `let scriptedRun = lastScriptedRun;` runs every tick, and the catch block clears `lastScriptedRun` on no path except a successful response with `run: null`. A 409 leaves it unchanged.","impact":"Example: the server closes the scripted run while the client still treats `scriptedEvent` as active (clock skew, early close, already participated → 409), or open keeps returning 5xx. For the rest of that event window, viewers see a frozen scripted run (stale tally/winner state) instead of host-launched manual runs and their updates. This only lasts until `scriptedEvent` changes, but it reverses the documented fallback behavior.","recommended_fix":"Reuse `lastScriptedRun` only when the POST was skipped because of `openRetryAt`, or when it just failed with 429/503. On any other failure (409, other non-OK statuses, network errors), set `lastScriptedRun = null` and `scriptedRun = null` so GET's manual runs are shown.","required_test":"Polling harness test: the first open returns 200 with run A. The next open returns 409 (and, separately, 500), while GET returns manual run B. Assert that `setRun` gets B on the following tick. Also assert that when open returns 429, `setRun` still gets A until the Retry-After delay ends.","confidence":0.6}]}
